easing_tokens_shared_css.s:
Goal: introduce the two premium easing tokens this project already uses inline (so the whole motion language shares one source of truth), then re-curve the shared CSS + the two champion components whose tests assert exact easing strings. Curve choices are NOT new numbers — they are copied verbatim from curves already shipping in this repo: `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` is used in PlatformCard.svelte, HomeAwards.svelte:250, +page.svelte:559 (the project's established premium deceleration curve, `--ease-out`); `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` is used in +page.svelte:613,776, HomeAwards.svelte:305 (the existing overshoot curve for playful scale moments, `--ease-spring`). Reusing existing in-repo curves keeps motion consistent instead of inventing numbers.

PHASE 1 — write the failing tests first. Three test files change; edit all three, then run `pnpm test` and confirm each fails for the stated reason before any implementation:

1a. src/styles/variables.test.ts — inside the existing `describe('variables.css design tokens', ...)`, add a new `it` right after the 'extends the spacing scale' block (after line 20):
```ts
  it('defines the premium easing tokens', () => {
    expect(css).toContain('--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1);');
    expect(css).toContain('--ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);');
  });
```
1b. src/lib/components/championship/ChampNav.test.ts line 22 — the 'animates the nav inner height alongside the scroll-condense' it currently asserts `expect(nav).toContain('transition: height 240ms ease;');`. Change the asserted string to `'transition: height 240ms var(--ease-out);'`. Everything else in that test file stays.
1c. src/lib/components/home/Footer.test.ts line 26 — the 'disables the hover transform transition under prefers-reduced-motion' it currently asserts `expect(footer).toContain('@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\n    .footer-nav a {\n      transition: color 160ms ease;\n    }\n  }');`. Change the inner line to `transition: color 160ms var(--ease-out);` (same 4-space indentation, same block shape).

PHASE 3 — implement, in order:

A. src/styles/variables.css — insert directly after line 3 (`  --noise-opacity: 0.03;`):
```css
  --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1);
  --ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
```
variables.css is imported by app.css (line 6) onto :root, so the tokens resolve in every component's scoped style block via CSS custom-property inheritance — no import changes needed anywhere.

B. src/styles/buttons.css:14 — old `transition: background-color 160ms ease, border-color 160ms ease, color 160ms ease, transform 160ms ease;` → new `transition: background-color 160ms var(--ease-out), border-color 160ms var(--ease-out), color 160ms var(--ease-out), transform 160ms var(--ease-out);` (hover `scale(1.02)`/active `scale(.98)` on .button-primary:23,27 now glide on the premium decel curve instead of the browser default).

C. src/styles/forms.css:137 — old `transition: border-color 160ms ease, box-shadow 160ms ease;` → new `transition: border-color 160ms var(--ease-out), box-shadow 160ms var(--ease-out);` (.text-input/.text-area focus ring). forms-modal.test.ts asserts the focus-visible rule block, which does NOT include this line — that test is untouched and stays green.

D. src/styles/navigation.css:47 — old `transition: width 200ms ease, height 200ms ease, border-radius 200ms ease;` → new `transition: width 200ms var(--ease-out), height 200ms var(--ease-out), border-radius 200ms var(--ease-out);` (.logo-chip). navigation.css:63 — old `transition: width 200ms ease, height 200ms ease;` → new `transition: width 200ms var(--ease-out), height 200ms var(--ease-out);` (.logo-chip img).

E. src/styles/cards.css — four lines. :16 old `transition: transform 240ms ease, box-shadow 240ms ease, background 240ms ease, border-color 240ms ease;` → `transition: transform 240ms var(--ease-out), box-shadow 240ms var(--ease-out), background 240ms var(--ease-out), border-color 240ms var(--ease-out);`. :35 old `transition: transform 240ms ease;` → `transition: transform 240ms var(--ease-out);` (.feature-card .spike-mark). :64 old `transition: opacity 0.6s ease, transform 0.6s ease, box-shadow 240ms ease, background 240ms ease, border-color 240ms ease;` → `transition: opacity 0.6s var(--ease-out), transform 0.6s var(--ease-out), box-shadow 240ms var(--ease-out), background 240ms var(--ease-out), border-color 240ms var(--ease-out);` (.benefit-card reveal). :173 old `transition: box-shadow 240ms ease;` → `transition: box-shadow 240ms var(--ease-out);` (.cta-card). cards.test.ts only asserts the hover box-shadow VALUE strings, the `@media (hover: hover)` gate, the spike-mark hover transform, the benefit-card transition COUNT (still 1 — one declaration), and the reduced-motion block; none change, so cards.test.ts is untouched and stays green.

F. src/lib/components/championship/ChampNav.svelte — five transition lines plus the bare-duration one. :96 old `transition: top 240ms ease, width 240ms ease;` → `transition: top 240ms var(--ease-out), width 240ms var(--ease-out);`. :215 old `transition: height 240ms ease;` → `transition: height 240ms var(--ease-out);`. :258 AND :321 are BOTH exactly `transition: background 160ms ease, color 160ms ease;` → `transition: background 160ms var(--ease-out), color 160ms var(--ease-out);` (use replaceAll in this file — it catches only these two identical lines). :272 old `transition: transform 220ms ease;` → `transition: transform 220ms var(--ease-out);` (.champ-nav-links a::after underline). :306 old `transition: opacity 0.2s;` → `transition: opacity 160ms var(--ease-out);` (.champ-nav-dash). :388 old `transition: transform 200ms ease;` → `transition: transform 200ms var(--ease-spring);` (.champ-mobile-btn span X-morph — the one spot where overshoot is right: a menu morph, not a color fade). Do NOT touch the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block (lines 114-126) which sets `transition: none` — that already matches ChampNav.test.ts's reduced-motion assertions. The sheen at :161 (`animation: sheen 5s ease-in-out infinite`) is an ambient loop, deliberately left on ease-in-out.

G. src/lib/components/home/Footer.svelte — :124 old `transition: color 160ms ease, transform 160ms ease;` → `transition: color 160ms var(--ease-out), transform 160ms var(--ease-out);`. :137 (inside the reduced-motion block), :167 (.footer-contact a), :183 (.footer-partner) are all exactly `transition: color 160ms ease;` → replaceAll to `transition: color 160ms var(--ease-out);` (three identical hits; :124 differs and is handled separately). The reduced-motion block intentionally keeps the color transition (only the hover transform is disabled) — that is the design intent the Footer.test.ts string encodes.

H. src/styles/animations.css:67 — old `animation: cta-entrance 600ms ease-out 1;` → new `animation: cta-entrance 600ms var(--ease-spring) 1;` (the one-shot CTA attention pulse now snaps on the project's overshoot curve; the reduced-motion kill-switch below it is unchanged).

PHASE 4 — run `pnpm test` (all green incl. the three updated files) and `pnpm check`. Why tokens over inline cubic-bezier everywhere: the two curves already float around the codebase as raw strings (PlatformCard, HomeAwards, +page.svelte:559/613/776, FaqAccordion:134) — this step anchors them as tokens so future edits (and the later steps) reference one name; existing inline uses are left untouched to keep this changeset minimal. Trap: do NOT use `var(--ease-out)` in the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` blocks' `transition: none` — those stay literal `none`.

copy_typos.s:
Root cause, established by probe: the ` , ` (space before comma) typo is SYSTEMIC — 60+ occurrences across the repo, from an IME/autocorrect habit. Fixing only the 5 originally-scoped lines would leave the same typo in FAQ answers, email subjects/bodies, alt text, screen-reader spans, and form copy. This step now fixes every USER-FACING occurrence (markup, copy, alt, sr-only, meta, email subjects/bodies, FAQ data, form strings) and the one test that asserts one of them. Server console logs and code comments that contain ` , ` are deliberately LEFT ALONE — they are invisible to users, and touching ~40 log/comment lines would churn the diff for zero user value. After this step, `rg -n " , " src` must return ONLY log/comment hits (verify each remaining hit is inside a `//` or `/* */` comment or a template-literal console.log/console.error/warn string). picsum_swap.s:
Replace every `https://picsum.photos/seed/...` placeholder with an already-existing local asset from this repo. Why: picsum is a third-party random-photo CDN — a production site should not depend on it at runtime (offline-unfriendly, arbitrary content, branded seed URLs in markup). All replacement files already exist under static/ (verified: static/images/technology-card.webp, static/images/enterprise.webp, static/images/bento-mentorship-candid.webp, static/images/championship/develop.webp, static/images/championship/learn.webp, static/flower-gear.webp, static/placeholder-user.jpg). Content precision is LOW-STAKES for all three components: each image renders as a grayscale, low-opacity background (`grayscale(0.6) contrast(1.2)` at `opacity: 0.1` in PillarsBento:120-124; `grayscale(0.25) contrast(1.1)` in TeamUpHero:131; `grayscale(0.3) contrast(1.1)` in PassportSection:150), so name/context-matched assets read as texture rather than subject. NOTE: this model cannot view images, so picks are made from file names + existing usage context — see the mapping notes.

PHASE 1 — failing probe: `rg -n picsum src` returns 7 matches (5 in PillarsBento:5-9, 1 in TeamUpHero:5, 1 in PassportSection:14). PHASE 2 = confirm. PHASE 3 — edit verbatim:

1. src/lib/components/teamup/PillarsBento.svelte lines 5-9, five `img:` values (context: the `pillars` data array; each entry is `{ l, n, d, img, g }`):
   - line 5 Technology: `img: 'https://picsum.photos/seed/tech/600/400',` → `img: '/images/technology-card.webp',` (technology-card.webp is ALREADY the Technology card image in ChampFeatures.svelte:5 — same pillar, consistent asset).
   - line 6 Enterprise: `img: 'https://picsum.photos/seed/enterprise/600/400',` → `img: '/images/enterprise.webp',` (ChampFeatures.svelte:11 uses it for the Enterprise card — same pillar).
   - line 7 Art: `img: 'https://picsum.photos/seed/art/600/400',` → `img: '/flower-gear.webp',` (the site's own abstract illustration mark, already shipped at static root and used in RegistrationForm.svelte:226 as the TEAMUP icon — the only on-brand abstract/design asset available; grayscale texture handles the zoom).
   - line 8 Mentorship: `img: 'https://picsum.photos/seed/mentor/600/400',` → `img: '/images/bento-mentorship-candid.webp',` (name-matched — candid mentorship photo, already used at +page.svelte:188).
   - line 9 Upskill: `img: 'https://picsum.photos/seed/skills/600/400',` → `img: '/images/championship/develop.webp',` (development/skills — ChampFeatures.svelte:23 uses develop.webp for its Develop stage; upskill == developing skills).
   Do NOT touch the `g:` gradient values on those lines.
2. src/lib/components/teamup/TeamUpHero.svelte:5 — `const hero_img = 'https://picsum.photos/seed/chess-education/1200/1400';` → `const hero_img = '/images/championship/learn.webp';` (learn.webp = child using the e4 AI chess coach — exact 'chess education' subject, per its alt text in HomeJourney.svelte:12).
3. src/lib/components/teamup/PassportSection.svelte:14 — `let passport_img = 'https://picsum.photos/seed/passport/800/600';` → `let passport_img = '/placeholder-user.jpg';` (a portrait placeholder is the closest existing asset to a passport-style identity photo; grayscale(0.3) + cover fit it to the frame).

If any chosen image proves visually wrong when a human views it later, swap only that entry to another existing static asset — but the mappings above are the committed picks. PHASE 4 — `rg -n picsum src` returns NOTHING; `pnpm test` + `pnpm check` green (no test asserts these URLs; PillarsBento/TeamUpHero/PassportSection have no string tests on the img values).

checklist_final_pass.s:
Final verification against the premium-web-design checklist, then ship. No code edits unless a probe finds a violation.

1. NO default easings remain on UI-response transitions. Probe: `rg -n "transition:.*(ease|0\.2s|0\.15s)|animation:.*ease-out" src --glob '*.svelte' --glob '*.css'`. Every hit must fall into one of the ALLOWED categories: (a) ambient LOOP animations on ease-in-out — ChampNav:161 sheen, TextInput:105 ti-sheen, PhoneInput:297 pi-sheen, hero.css:266 drift, theme.css:30-33 --animate-* vars, payment/callback/+page.svelte:104 pulse, design/+page.svelte:797 button-pulse (loop easing is the premium choice, same principle as the linear marquee); (b) one-shot entrances already re-curved or GSAP-driven (Modal, HomeJourney, ChampAbout:75, quotes:419/429); (c) `transition: none` reduced-motion kills. Anything else = fix it in this step.
2. ZERO `transition: all`. Probe: `rg -n "transition: all" src` → nothing.
3. ZERO bare `0.2s`/`0.15s` transitions (all normalized to 150-300ms + curve). Probe: `rg -n "transition:.*0\.2s|transition:.*0\.15s" src` → nothing.
4. Interactive hover still has matching focus. base.css:45,50-51 already has a global `:focus-visible` rule for a/button/input (verified) — so every re-curved hover target inherits a keyboard-focus state; confirm that rule remains intact (don't delete it).
5. Reduced-motion guards intact. Probe: `rg -n "prefers-reduced-motion" src/styles src/lib/components/championship/ChampNav.svelte src/lib/components/home/Footer.svelte src/lib/components/faq/FaqAccordion.svelte` — every block that killed a transform under reduced motion must still exist; Footer's block intentionally keeps the color-only transition (per its test), ChampNav keeps `transition: none`.
6. No stray picsum/production-host leaks. Probe: `rg -n "picsum" src` → nothing. `rg -n "localhost|127\.0\.0\.1" src/lib/components src/styles` → nothing new.
7. Full gate: `pnpm test` (entire suite — cards/forms-modal/variables/ChampNav/Footer/quotes must all pass) then `pnpm check` (svelte-kit sync + svelte-check).

If every probe is clean, this step's work is done. If a probe catches a violation, fix it with the same verbatim-editing discipline as the earlier steps, re-run the probes + gate, and note in the final message exactly what was caught and fixed. This step also confirms the global scope change is complete — the motion language of the whole site now reads off two easing tokens, all copy typos are gone, the font payload is trimmed, and no third-party placeholder images ship.
